hook: Richard Sutton studied psychology at Stanford before moving into computer science at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where he earned his PhD in 1984 working with Andrew Barto on the mathematical foundations of reinforcement learning. He went on to research positions in industry and academia before joining the University of Alberta, where he now holds the AITF Chair in Reinforcement Learning and Artificial Intelligence and serves as Chief Scientific Advisor to the Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute. With Barto he wrote Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, the field's standard textbook, first published in 1998 and revised in 2018. He also holds a part-time research role at Google DeepMind and in 2022 helped found Keen Technologies with John Carmack to pursue artificial general intelligence. His 2019 essay The Bitter Lesson argued that general, computation-driven learning methods outperform approaches built on human-designed domain knowledge, a claim that shaped much of the field's later direction. In 2024 he and Barto received the ACM A.M. Turing Award for developing the conceptual and algorithmic foundations of reinforcement learning.
name: Richard Sutton

quote.text: The biggest lesson that can be read from 70 years of AI research is that general methods that leverage computation are ultimately the most effective, and by a large margin.
